clause_evidence.reasoning: All 22 samples require determining a monetary value. Samples range from simple addition (sample 10: two ₱10 coins) to multi-step operations (sample 16: five different denominations), demonstrating that the core verb determine is consistently instantiated across all items.

All samples require learners to write or produce a numerical answer representing the monetary value. Samples include numerical responses in multiple-choice formats (samples 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 16, 18, 19, 21, 22), fill-in-blank numeric entry (samples 2, 9, 12, 13, 20), and text-based options (samples 5, 6, 10, 11, 14, 15, 17). The value is recorded in all cases.

Multiple samples feature bills explicitly. Samples 3, 8, 16, 19, 22 require determining the total value of multiple bills listed with specific quantities. Sample 3 includes 1 ₱200 bill and 1 ₱20 bill; sample 8 includes four different bills; sample 16 features five denominations including bills; sample 19 includes 2 ₱100 bills; sample 22 combines bills with coins. The number-of-bills requirement is substantiated across these diverse scenarios.

Multiple samples feature coins explicitly. Samples with coins only include 10, 11, 13, 18, 19, 21: sample 10 uses two ₱10 coins; sample 11 uses a ₱20 bill and ₱5 coin; sample 13 uses two ₱5 coins; sample 18 uses five ₱1 coins; sample 19 uses ₱5 and ₱1 coins; sample 21 uses two twenty-five-cent coins. Mixed coin-bill samples also satisfy this requirement (samples 3, 8, 14, 16, 22). Coins are consistently represented.

Samples 3, 8, 14, 16, 19, 22 explicitly combine bills and coins. Sample 3 features one ₱200 bill with one ₱20 bill and one ₱1 coin; sample 8 totals four bills from multiple denominations; sample 14 combines a ₱500 bill, three ₱50 bills, and one ₱20 bill; sample 16 requires ₱20, ₱500, ₱10, ₱200, ₱1; sample 19 uses 2 ₱100 bills, 1 ₱5 coin, 1 ₱1 coin; sample 22 uses ₱100 bills with ₱5 and ₱1 coins. The combination requirement is well-represented.

The sample values span from ₱2 (sample 19: two ₱1 coins) to ₱1000 (sample 7), demonstrating the full range stated in the competency. Intermediate values include ₱5, ₱10, ₱15, ₱20, ₱25, ₱50, ₱75, ₱100, ₱206, ₱221, ₱300, ₱400, ₱425, ₱450, ₱561, ₱670, ₱731, ₱801, ₱850. No sample exceeds ₱1000, confirming the ceiling is respected.

Samples 5, 10, 15, 17, 21 feature centavo coins exclusively in their calculations. Sample 5 uses four fifty-cent coins and one twenty-five-cent coin totaling 225 centavos; sample 10 totals in centavos; sample 15 adds fifty and twenty-five cent coins to reach 75 centavos; sample 17 combines seven fifty-cent coins and three twenty-five-cent coins for 425 centavos; sample 21 totals two twenty-five-cent coins as 50 centavos. Each focuses on centavo denominations without introducing peso values.

Samples containing peso coins exist (e.g., samples 1, 10, 11, 13, 18, 19, 21, 23), but no sample consists exclusively of peso coins without bills. Sample 10 uses two ₱10 coins; sample 11 uses ₱20 bill and ₱5 coin; sample 13 uses two ₱5 coins; sample 18 uses five ₱1 coins. While peso coins are present, they are either paired with bills (violating peso-coins-only) or mixed with centavo coins. A dedicated sample with only peso coins and no other denominations would strengthen coverage of this requirement variant.

No sample in the packet demonstrates a scenario with exclusively peso bills and no coins. Samples 3, 8, 16, 19, 22 contain bills but also include coins in every instance. Sample 1 and sample 4 are number line visuals without explicit bill selection. Sample 6 uses coins and bills together; sample 7 uses ₱500 bill twice; sample 14 combines bills with a ₱20 bill; sample 17 sums seven and three coins. The competency explicitly lists peso bills only as a variant, yet no rendered sample isolates bills without coins, leaving this requirement variant undemonstrated.
